summary: Garbled prefix on SSE resume causes parser failure in client SDK
description:
Issue summary:

Customer reports that after an SSE disconnect/resume sequence the client SDK receives an extra garbled byte-prefix at the start of the resumed payload. The SDK JSON parser fails on that first chunk, leading to a partial/incomplete final response visible to the end user.

Impact:
- Persistent failed completions for long-lived streams when a short disconnect happens (mobile/browser backgrounding, edge failover).
- Affects multiple customers on Dedicated clusters behind our edge proxy in us-east.
- Observable as 'Unexpected token' parsing errors in the client SDK and truncated final choices returned to the app.

Observed behavior:
- Initial SSE stream starts normally and emits partial tokens as expected.
- Short network hiccup (~1–3s) leads to client reconnect to resume session.
- The first resumed chunk begins with non-JSON prefix bytes (visible as \u0000 or binary fragments) before the valid JSON payload.
- SDK's internal parser throws and surface to application as incomplete final_choice.

Why this ticket is different from previous resume issues: the corrupt bytes appear to be a buffer residue (prefix) rather than missing end/end markers or split tokens. The corruption is deterministic for the customer's environment and reproduces consistently when their edge path includes a particular third-party proxy appliance.
steps_to_reproduce: Start a long-running SSE generation from the hosted API with streaming enabled and client SDK v2.3.1.
Simulate a short network interruption (e.g., background tab, mobile network switch) for ~1-3 seconds.
Allow client SDK to perform an automatic resume via the session token and observe the first resumed chunk payload delivered to the SDK parser.
Repeat behind customer's edge proxy or reproduce in test lab using tcpdump + mitm proxy that reuses connection buffer pools.
Observe JSON parser error in SDK logs and truncated final output in the application UI.
logs: [2026-03-10T14:12:07Z] STREAM: connection lost, attempt resume token=eyJr...
[2026-03-10T14:12:09Z] CLIENT-SDK: JSON parse error: Unexpected token \u0000 in JSON at position 0
tcpdump snippet: sequence shows leftover buffer bytes (0x00 0x1f) preceding the first application frame after resume
investigation_notes: Customer environment uses an inline L4 appliance that performs connection pooling and may reuse small internal buffers when handing sockets between worker threads.
Edge proxy (internal) logs show successful resume handshake and no TCP retransmits around the event timestamp.
Reproduced locally by configuring a proxy that deliberately injects a two-byte null prefix into the first resumed frame; SDK fails to recover (v2.3.1).
Hypothesis 1: upstream edge/proxy is emitting residual buffer prefix on resumed streams due to a pooling bug; bytes are accidental and not part of framing protocol.
Hypothesis 2: our SDK resume handler does not strictly strip non-printable leading bytes before JSON parse; other SDKs may be tolerant and silently trim leading control bytes.
Observed that some clients using raw fetch/EventSource are more tolerant (browser automatically ignores) while our SDK's strict JSON.parse fails.
resolution: Workaround provided to customer: 1) update customer SDK to v2.3.2 (hotfix branch) which trims leading control bytes before parsing; 2) recommend bypassing third-party inline proxy or disable buffer pooling on appliance as a long-term mitigation. Engineering action: serving-runtime team will add an additional validation layer at the API edge to reject or sanitize resumed frames that start with non-UTF8/control bytes. Patch PR created and under review (see related_github_prs).
